proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the proposed value transfer, finite LP brackets, and strict privacy-cost result; the math referee passed. The field-tier contribution did not survive D0.5 because no complete audited rational certificate or reproducible refinement run was delivered, and the quantitative example used an extreme privacy budget and intensity. The two comparator-positioning findings remain open. A future re-raise needs a certified numerical receipt and evidence at conventional privacy budgets and genuinely small treated counts.
tldr: For the legal finite-sample domain \(n>\lambda_{\max}\), treatment probabilities are \(\lambda_x/n\) and the treated sample remains of constant order, so regular private ATT Wald theory does not determine the best honest interval. The exact eventual-sample-size all-mechanism expected-length value is the marked-Poisson confidence game with the full add-delete-substitute record graph. A finite randomized-interval program gives convergent two-sided bounds, and the theorem gives conditional outward error propagation from any independently verified rational primal-dual receipts. Full-record privacy strictly increases the value on a nonempty open set of legal constants. No concrete complete audited receipt or shrinking refinement sequence is currently supplied.
gap: Published private causal intervals treat regular WATE or ATE regimes, while exact private binomial intervals hold the count fixed. Neither literature determines the decision value when treatment membership is sensitive and only finitely many treated records survive asymptotically.
fill: A graph-preserving two-way transfer identifies the limiting value without weakening privacy or coverage, a finite LP provides convergent two-sided bounds, and exact arithmetic receipts make the benchmark independently auditable.
